History:
• 24-hour history of a “really bad,” throbbing headache, first noted on waking yesterday morning  
• Location: predominantly left-sided  
• Character: throbbing, intense, fluctuates but never fully resolves  
• Photophobia present; prefers dark room  
• No nausea, vomiting, visual changes, abnormal smells/tastes, fever, cough, rhinorrhea, sore ears, skin changes, limb weakness, tingling, or numbness  
• Pain improves when lying down; worsens with bright light; no clear positional, cough, or sneeze exacerbation  
• No prior history of headaches or migraines  
• Last menstrual period ~1 week ago; no cyclical association reported  
• Possible trigger: recent work-related stress  
• Self-care to date: paracetamol (dose not documented); has avoided aspirin due to allergy

Past Medical History:
• No significant past illnesses, hospitalizations, or surgeries reported  
• Medications:  
  – Microgynon oral contraceptive pill, dose/frequency not documented  
  – Paracetamol (acetaminophen) as needed for headache, dose/frequency not documented  
• Allergies: Aspirin – causes severe nausea  
• Family history: Mother with hypertension and migraines  
• Social: Non-smoker; social alcohol (few drinks on weekends); denies recreational drugs; lives with housemates

Physical Examination:
(History-based teleconsultation; no direct examination)  
• Patient reports being alert, oriented, eating and drinking well  
• No self-reported fever; temperature not measured  
• No visual disturbances, focal neurological deficits, or skin rashes by history  
• No throat swelling; no respiratory or ENT symptoms

Impression:
New-onset unilateral throbbing headache with photophobia, most consistent with a first episode migraine.

Management Plan:
• Start NSAID (e.g., Ibuprofen) in addition to paracetamol for acute pain relief (specific dose/route/frequency not documented)  
• Emphasize good oral hydration  
• Safety-net advice: seek immediate review if headache worsens, changes character, is accompanied by fever, rash, or other new symptoms  
• Arrange blood pressure check at earliest convenience  
• Obtain a home thermometer to monitor temperature during illness  
• Re-evaluate if headaches become persistent, cyclical, or refractory to over-the-counter therapy

Patient Summary:
The patient presents with a 1-day history of a new, left-sided throbbing headache with photophobia and no red-flag features. Clinical picture most closely resembles a migraine. She will trial combined paracetamol and NSAID therapy, ensure hydration, and have her blood pressure checked.

Key Takeaways:
• Begin Ibuprofen with paracetamol and stay well-hydrated.  
• Monitor for worsening pain, fever, rash, or any new neurological symptoms—seek care immediately if they occur.  
• Arrange a routine blood pressure check and consider obtaining a home thermometer.

Next Steps:
• Patient to obtain NSAID today and commence therapy  
• Schedule blood pressure measurement within the next few days (e.g., local pharmacy or GP nurse)  
• Follow-up consultation if no improvement in 48–72 hours or sooner if red-flag symptoms develop
